newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Banco Real aims to expand credit in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Banco Real aims to expand credit in 1997.

text.p: Brazil's Banco Real aims to expand its credit operations in 1997 as corporate and consumer defaults, which reached high levels and harmed banks in the past two years, appear to have stabilized, said a bank executive.
"We can be more aggressive in our credit operations as we consider that corporate and consumer loan defaults are now under control," said Rene Aduan, director at Banco Real.
Aduan said the private bank's bad debts portfolio totalled 164.2 million reais at the end of March and those debts were covered by loan loss provisions of 238.9 million reais.

Banco Real posted a net profit of 50.124 million reais in the first quarter, showing an annualized 13 percent return on equity. Aduan said a combination of factors contributed to the bank's first quarter earnings, including its corporate finance activities, credit operations and an increase in deposits, savings accounts and investment funds.

The Banco Real director also said the bank wants to expand its client base, which has already increased from 1.5 million 15 months ago to 2.4 million full clients. The number of current account holders rose to 1.9 million from one million in the period.
"Our idea is to reach 2.2 million current account holders and 2.7 million full clients by the end of the year," he said.

Aduan said Banco Real does not fear stiffer competition in Brazil's retail banking, even though local banks, including Banco Excel Economico and BCN, decided to follow Real's example and offer clients up to a certain number of days of interest-free credit for overdrafts.

Real, which is among Brazil's 10 largest private banks, offers up to 10 days of interest-free credit for overdrafts; Excel Economico guarantees 12 days; and more recently BCN began to offer up to 18 days.
Aduan said the bank's strategy to increase its client base includes to improve banking services and to "offer interesting products for individuals and corporate customers."
